Header: Puccinia sorghi Amharic: ye bekelo wag; Tigrigna: nay efun humodya

Prevention: Deep plough crop residue after harvest
Use of clean maize seed from a reliable source
Plant maize in rows in the direction of prevailing winds for maximum air circulation
Rotate maize crop with non- cereal crops at least every 2-3 years (beans, fababean, chickpea etc.)
Monitoring: Monitor the plant every week, especially when there are favourable environmental conditions (humid conditions and wind that can aggravate the common rust on maize)
Start to observe the maize plant after 6 leaves emerge until the tasseling stage
In the early stage of the disease, look for small chlorotic areas developing on the leaves.
These turn into elongated and scattered dark red, brownish pustules on both the upper and lower side of the leaves
Pustules may also appear on husks, tassels and stalks
Carry out controls as soon as the first symptoms are seen
Direct Control: Remove lower leaves which are infested to improve air circulation and reduce the inoculum (traces of fungi).
Destroy the infected leaves by burning
When removing infected leaves always start working from the healthy part of the field before moving to the infected part of the field
Restrictions: There are no chemical pesticides registered in
Ethiopia at this time for common rust on maize
